questions.stem: In a KQL query over a table of sensor events, which operator keeps only the rows where Temperature > 80?
questions.explanation: where filters a table to the subset of rows that satisfy a predicate.

questions.stem: You want every column of Events plus a new column TempF computed from TempC. Which operator?
questions.explanation: extend creates calculated columns and appends them, keeping the input's columns. project with only TempF would drop every other column.

questions.stem: Which query counts events per hour?
questions.explanation: summarize aggregates the input table, and bin rounds values down to a multiple of the bin size, so each hour becomes one group. Grouping by Timestamp alone makes a group per distinct time.

questions.stem: What does project DeviceId, Temperature do?

options.text: Keeps only DeviceId and Temperature, dropping every other column
Adds DeviceId and Temperature as new columns next to all the others
Sorts the rows by DeviceId and then by Temperature
Groups the rows by DeviceId and averages Temperature

questions.explanation: Only the columns named in project's arguments are included in the result; any other columns are dropped.

questions.stem: Someone uses Events | take 10 to see 'the latest ten events'. What's wrong?

options.text: take returns up to ten rows with no guarantee which ones, unless the data is sorted
take returns the ten oldest rows, because it reads the table in ingestion order
take needs a by clause naming the column to pick the ten rows by
Nothing: take always returns the ten rows with the latest timestamp

questions.explanation: take returns up to the specified number of rows, and there's no guarantee which records are returned unless the source data is sorted.
